title: divide() crashes on a zero denominator
issue:
divide() raises ZeroDivisionError when the denominator is zero.

The reporting pipeline calls calculator.divide() with data-derived denominators, and a zero denominator is an ordinary occurrence, not an error. When it happens the whole report crashes:

    Traceback (most recent call last):
      File "pipeline.py", line 42, in build_report
        ratio = divide(part, whole)
      File "src/calculator.py", line 24, in divide
        return a / b
    ZeroDivisionError: division by zero

Expected behaviour: divide() should return None when the denominator is zero, which is what its docstring and type hint (float | None) already promise. percentage() should then propagate that None.

Observed behaviour: it raises ZeroDivisionError.

Reproduce with: python -m pytest tests/test_calculator.py -q
notes: Single-function guard clause. The docstring and return type already state the intended contract, so the fix is unambiguous.
